description: CleanManager host commands for the main window. No shell, fs, opener or dialog permissions are exposed to the WebView; folder picking (scan roots, purge roots) happens in Rust and returns an opaque token or root id. No command accepts a filesystem path or a plan body: plans, operations, quarantine items and policies are named by store-issued ids, and approval needs a host-issued review token plus the typed digest prefix. Software, maintenance and process commands take app, operation, leftover, task, download-item ids or a PID; every change they make is a stored plan pending the same review (including putting back a maintenance run's setting changes), and open_system_page opens only fixed system pages (Windows: Settings › Apps or the Store's updates page; macOS: Storage, the App Store's updates, Login Items or Software Update settings). AI diagnosis commands take scan/entry/preview/diagnosis ids only; provider keys are entered in the system credential prompt and never cross IPC. Resident utilities (状态 › 常驻工具) read status, privacy and battery state; their only writes are CleanManager's resident.json, on Windows the CleanManager-owned HKCU Run value CleanManager.Resident (opt-in, removed when the tray is turned off; on macOS start at login is refused and nothing is written), a temporary keep-awake request (Windows power request, macOS IOPMAssertion) and the time-limited clean-screen window. Release gates (D15): every command of a capability whose gate has not passed is refused before it runs unless experimental features are on; set_experimental_features writes only CleanManager's features.json, and turning it off stops the resident utilities and removes their startup value (Windows). clean_catalog (the cleanup catalog page) only reads the rule pack, checks whether rule locations exist (home folder never sent) and reads a stored analysis of a named scan; it changes nothing. Every command reaches the same Windows or macOS backend as the matching cleanmanager CLI command.
